title: “I Would Never Trust Anything Western”: Kumu (Educator) Perspectives on Use of LLMs for Culturally Revitalizing CS Education in Hawaiian Schools
benchmark_measurement: The paper qualitatively explores the misalignment of LLMs with Indigenous Hawaiian cultural values, epistemologies, and moʻolelo (stories/legends), which encompass spiritual and faith-based beliefs. It measures educator perceptions of AI's potential for cultural misrepresentation and the perpetuation of a 'colonized perspective.'
findings: The key finding related to faith and spirituality is that educators are deeply concerned that LLMs, trained on Western data, fail to grasp and accurately represent Indigenous Hawaiian epistemology (ways of knowing). They fear AI will misinterpret sacred stories (moʻolelo) and cultural values, presenting a colonized view that could harm cultural revitalization efforts. Educators feel AI-generated content defaults to a Western perspective and requires significant effort to align with an Indigenous worldview, which is often intertwined with spiritual beliefs and a connection to the land ('āina).
